findings.criterion: Unresolved bug candidate: e57f-200d-d402-4a5e — Agentic plan review signs a PASS with zero tool calls
findings.detail: This is an open bug in the epic's own agentic engine (`agentic_verdict.adapt_findings` and the `agentic_review` step). It says an agent that answers `{"findings": []}` with no read_file/list_directory/search_files calls gets a non-blocking PASS and a certified attestation that the claim gate accepts. The epic's fail-closed invariant says only a clean, completed run yields PASS. The bug has no `supersedes` or `duplicates` link and no deferral or successor rationale in the ticket snapshot I read. The epic's own handoff comment lists it as an advisory (b) 'not filed here', which is not a disposition. It is unfinished work on the epic's deliverable.
findings.remediation: Fix it (a 0-tool-call run resolves INDETERMINATE and the coverage records the tool-call count) and close the bug. Alternatively, record a reasoned deferral or successor on the bug, with a link.

findings.criterion: Unresolved bug candidate: 5bd7-33ec-8630-440e — Agentic verdicts skip drift floor and cross-checks
findings.detail: This is an open bug in the epic's `_run_plan_review` dispatch. Under the agentic engine the post-dispatch tail is skipped: the rising, completion and drift floors, `xcheck` and fix-unit grouping. The two engines can therefore sign different verdict strings and blocking lists for the same plan and findings. It also says ADR 0123 does not document that the tail is pipeline-only. The epic requires the same verdict contract on both engines and an ADR that records the design. The bug has no recorded disposition in the snapshot I read. The epic's handoff comment lists it as advisory (a) and says it was not filed.
findings.remediation: Run the tail on agentic verdicts, or amend ADR 0123 to state and justify that it is pipeline-only. Pin the chosen behavior with a test under both engines and close the bug.

findings.criterion: Unresolved bug candidate: ac9f-db05-bc10-41a0 — Old-generation model ids in src/rebar defaults
findings.detail: This is an open bug in the model upgrade the epic delivered (Goal 3, 'upgrade every configured model'). Two hard-coded defaults still name the 4.x generation: `registry.chunk_by_facet` defaults to `claude-sonnet-4-6`, and `fixture_emit._MODEL` is `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`. The bug has no recorded disposition in the snapshot I read. The epic's handoff comment lists it as advisory (d) and says it was not filed.
findings.remediation: Remove the old-generation defaults and add the guard test the bug asks for, then close the bug. Alternatively, record a reasoned deferral that explains why these defaults are outside the upgrade.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, the criterion needs the exact `[non-codebase]` tag at the start of the checkbox text, `- [ ] [non-codebase] <criterion>`, and an indented continuation line directly under it, `provenance: environment=<v>; principal=<v>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower>; instrument=<live-call|simulation|static-analysis> — <justification>`. If the reviewed plan did not already carry both, add them in one description edit: that edit changes the reviewed plan and stales the plan-review attestation, so run `rebar review-plan` on this ticket before closing again. Then add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet the criterion (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion); comments are non-material, so a criterion tagged before review needs only the comment. The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
